scenario: AITA for calling the police on my daughter to teach her a lesson about stealing? | My daughter is in the sixth grade. Every morning, I have her take a couple of dollars out of my wallet for lunch money. In the last few weeks, several times I have noticed that I am missing a little bit more money than usual. So, this week, I planted a 20 dollar bill before my daughter took her lunch money out. Sure enough, she took it. I called the police and asked them to come with me to the school so that we could teach my daughter a lesson. Two officers met me there and we pulled my daughter out of class, after which she informed one of the officers that there has been a bully who is stealing her lunch money/forcing my daughter to buy her lunch. She also has been buying lunch for one of her friends who can not afford it. This was confirmed by both the bully, and the friend. My daughter was silent on the way home and i informed her that I was just trying to teach her a lesson, that stealing is wrong and can get you in a lot of trouble. and that in the future she needs to speak to myself or her mother if there are issues at school and we would be happy to help her resolve them. When we got home, my wife absolutely lost her shit on me, in full tears, telling me that this is a one way ticket to estrangement from our daughter in the future and that we should have just asked her why she was stealing money. She would have just lied about stealing in the first place so I really don’t understand what her idea of a solution is. My daughter apparently told my wife that she is terrified that her bully will now retaliate, and also that she may have lost her friend for bringing so much attention to her financial issue. She apologized for stealing and said she just didn’t want us to intervene. I am wondering if I really did the wrong thing here. AITA?

Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. Let me start by understanding the situation.

The parent is a mother of a sixth-grade daughter. Every morning, the daughter takes a couple of dollars from the mother's wallet for lunch money. Recently, the mother noticed that more money was missing than usual. To catch the daughter, she planted a $20 bill and sure enough, the daughter took it. The mother then called the police, and they went to the school to confront the daughter. 

When they pulled the daughter out of class, she told the officers that there was a bully stealing her lunch money and forcing her to buy lunch for the bully. She also mentioned that she was buying lunch for a friend who couldn't afford it. Both the bully and the friend confirmed this. The daughter was silent on the way home, and the mother explained that she was trying to teach her a lesson about stealing and the consequences. She also told her daughter to come to her or her wife if there are issues at school in the future.

When they got home, the wife was upset, crying, and told the mother that this action could lead to estrangement from their daughter. The wife suggested that they should have just asked the daughter why she was stealing instead of involving the police. The daughter told the wife that she was scared the bully would retaliate and that she might have lost her friend because of the attention brought to her financial issue. The daughter apologized for stealing and said she didn't want her parents to intervene.

Now, the question is: Was the mother's action morally acceptable? Let's break this down.

First, the mother noticed that more money was missing than usual. She suspected her daughter of stealing. To confirm, she planted a $20 bill and caught her daughter taking it. Then, she called the police to confront her daughter at school. 

On the surface, the mother's intention was to teach her daughter a lesson about stealing and the consequences. She wanted her daughter to understand that stealing is wrong and could lead to trouble. She also wanted to encourage her daughter to come to her or her wife if there are issues at school instead of handling them on her own.

However, the way she went about it involved calling the police and confronting her daughter at school. This action led to the daughter being pulled out of class, which could have been embarrassing or stressful for her. Additionally, the daughter revealed that she was being bullied and had to buy lunch for a friend who couldn't afford it. This means that the daughter was taking extra money to help her friend and possibly to deal with the bully.

The mother's action led to the daughter feeling scared about potential retaliation from the bully and possibly losing a friend because of the attention brought to her financial situation. The daughter apologized and expressed that she didn't want her parents to intervene.

The wife was upset, feeling that this action could damage the relationship with their daughter. She suggested that they should have talked to the daughter first instead of involving the police.

So, considering all this, was the mother's action morally acceptable?

I think it's important to consider the intent versus the method. The mother's intent was to teach her daughter a lesson about stealing and to encourage open communication. However, the method she chose involved involving the police and confronting the daughter at school, which led to unintended consequences, such as the daughter feeling scared and possibly losing a friend.

Moreover, the daughter was taking extra money to help her friend and deal with a bully, which adds another layer to the situation. The mother didn't know about the bullying and the financial help for the friend until after confronting her daughter.

In this case, the mother's action might have been too harsh and could have been handled differently. Instead of involving the police, she could have talked to her daughter first to understand why she was taking extra money. This approach would have allowed her to address the underlying issues, such as the bullying and the financial help for the friend, in a more supportive way.

By involving the police, the mother created a stressful situation for her daughter, which could have negative long-term effects on their relationship. It also didn't address the root cause of why the daughter was taking extra money.

Therefore, while the mother's intent was to teach a lesson, the method she used was not the most appropriate. It led to unintended negative consequences and could have been handled in a more supportive and understanding way.
